solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Model puts many years in to steal the show

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

parts.note: an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A fashion model gains years of experience and ends up stealing the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal, used as a verb meaning shape; 'in' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to draw attention away from them, taking the limelight.

clue.text: A French orphan is free of entanglements

parts.note: un is the French for a
Oliver Twist is Dickens's famous orphan

explanation.surface: A French orphan has no ties or complications in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orphan' points to Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'is' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwist is to unwind and release something from knots and tangles.

clue.text: Unwanted fat found in rolls we're told

definitions.text: Unwanted fat found in rolls we're told

parts.words: Unwanted fat found in rolls we're told
parts.note: rolls of flab round the waist, and also the spare wheel carried in a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the excess flab collecting in rolls around the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The roll of fat round the waist is nicknamed after the extra wheel a car carries, and a Rolls (Rolls-Royce) would carry one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is the colloquial name for a roll of excess fat around the waist.

clue.text: Relax in a club, mid-September

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket

indicators.note: mid asks for the centre letter of the word September

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds at a club in the middle of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a place to relax but is a bat; 'in' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or ease off, as tension relaxes.

clue.text: A name I'll confuse with English battle

indicators.note: to confuse is to jumble, so the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a name might be muddled with an English battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuse' rearranges A NAME I'LL into LALAMEIN, which follows E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of a decisive Second World War battle in 1942.

clue.text: Single person's favourite kind of convenience store

parts.note: one's means a person's, single being one
the top choice is the favourite

explanation.surface: A singleton's favourite place to shop is the local convenience store.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as ONE'S TOP: a person's top choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-stop shop sells everything a customer needs in a single place.

clue.text: Group extremely eloquent after a month

indicators.note: after places the eloquent piece behind the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: extremely asks for the end letters of the word eloquent

explanation.surface: A group of people speaking very eloquently a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially musicians.

clue.text: Dramatic eastern proposal the French rejected

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

indicators.note: rejected means the French article is turned back

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A theatrical proposal from the East is turned down by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional behaviour is highly charged and theatrical, much like a dramatic scene.

clue.text: Crime you have in hand!

parts.note: ..., the Financial Times, is the paper the solver is holding

explanation.surface: An accusation that the reader is holding stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THE FT: the solver of this Financial Times puzzle literally has the FT in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the crime of taking another's property, and the paper in hand is the Financial Times.

clue.text: Pilots trained on top secret weapons

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order
top asks for the first letter of the word secret

explanation.surface: Pilots are trained in the use of top-secret weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top secret' reads as a phrase but 'top' takes S; 'on' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols are handguns, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Headdress, one buried in Ireland's royal site

indicators.note: buried in places the numeral inside the place name

parts.note: the Hill of Tara was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A headdress has been found buried at an ancient Irish royal site.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Christie possibly organised shareouts

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie arranged for the profits to be distributed.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie is an example of a female author, so 'possibly' marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie was a female writer, an old-fashioned term for which uses a feminine suffix.

clue.text: Line breaks down, say, worker being clumsy

indicators.note: breaks down suggests the word line falls apart and is rebuilt

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A production line breaks down because a worker is careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' turns LINE into INEL; 'being' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or polish, which is awkward and ungainly.

clue.text: Italian leader leaves to present musical opening

indicators.note: leaves means the leader's title departs from the longer word

parts.note: to present someone is to introduce them
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist leader

explanation.surface: An Italian leader walks out just as a performance is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: DUCE is Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the short opening passage of a song or piece of music.

clue.text: Season, we hear, for seasoning

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: A cook asks which time of year suits a particular herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a verb of cooking, but it is a noun for a period of time; 'for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used to flavour food.

clue.text: Cockney festival about to finish

indicators.note: about means the festival goes round the other piece

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A London festival is about to come to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner; an East Ender lives in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: East Enders, people from London's East End, are the traditional Cockneys.

clue.text: Leads to sex in various quarters

indicators.note: in means the sex word sits inside the compass points

parts.note: E, N and S are compass points, the quarters of the compass
gender is a synonym for sex

explanation.surface: Sex is the cause of trouble in different parts of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to cause or give rise to something.

clue.text: They may well be read below stairs

definitions.text: They may well be read below stairs

parts.words: They may well be read below stairs
parts.note: devices in a cellar or under the stairs are read by a meter reader, not books read by servants

explanation.surface: Servants below stairs might well read these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below stairs' suggests the servants' quarters and reading books, but these devices measure fuel in a basement or under the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas meters record domestic gas use and are often fitted in a cupboard under the stairs.

clue.text: Pit in live broadcast closes in year, it seems

indicators.note: closes in means the whole thing ends with the year
in places the pit inside the scrambled word
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: a dent is a small pit or hollow in a surface

explanation.surface: A mine pit appears in a live broadcast that closes within the year, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns the fodder into EVIL, with the pit placed after its third letter; 'closes in year' puts Y at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidently means apparently or seemingly, as the evidence suggests.

clue.text: Game that's hard, which country folk accept

indicators.note: accept means the country folk take the letter inside

parts.note: peasants are rural people
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Country people take on a tough game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' and 'which' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are game birds shot for sport and food.

clue.text: It could be first-class when Gestapo gets involved

indicators.note: gets involved suggests the letters become entangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something first-rate happens when the Nazi secret police step in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'first-class' as a stamp tier, not as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class postage is the faster, dearer tier of postal charge in Britain.

clue.text: Places to hide from penniless landlords

indicators.note: penniless means the d for an old penny is removed

parts.note: lairds are Scottish landowners

explanation.surface: Somewhere to hide from landlords when one has no money for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the old British penny (from the Latin denarius). 'from' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairs are dens where animals or fugitives lie hidden.

clue.text: Pioneer Crux eg takes control, finally

indicators.note: takes means the setter holds the letter inside

parts.note: Crux is the setter of this puzzle

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word control

explanation.surface: A pioneering puzzle maker seizes command at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is a pioneer who colonises new land.

clue.text: Husband admits love for Italian wine

indicators.note: admits means the verb lets the letter in

parts.note: to husband is to save or conserve resources
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A husband confesses his love of an Italian wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a man but is the verb meaning to save; 'for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto region of Italy.

clue.text: A charming accent

parts.note: cute means charming or attractive

explanation.surface: Someone has an attractive way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a written accent mark, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is the diacritical mark slanting up to the right, as in é.

clue.text: High as can be and still seem stupid!

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are senselessly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs still looks dopey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' suggests being intoxicated, but here it means smelling strongly, as gamey meat does; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is high gives off a strong odour, so the highest is the most pungent.

clue.text: It indicates strength in exotic wines

indicators.note: exotic means unusual, so the letters are put in an outlandish order

explanation.surface: The strength of foreign wines is indicated on the label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew stands for muscular strength and toughness.

clue.text: Romeo (or Juliet) left for dead in port

indicators.note: for means the left letter takes the place of the dead one

parts.note: Dover is a port on the English Channel

explanation.surface: Romeo, or Juliet, is left for dead in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are the archetypal pair of romantic partners; 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet are Shakespeare's emblematic sweethearts, each devoted to the other.

clue.text: A knees-up with cake eaten in plenty

indicators.note: eaten in means the cake goes inside the party

parts.note: a knees-up is a lively British party with dancing
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A lively party with cake on offer means there is food in abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a plentiful supply of something.

clue.text: Key WW2 missile the army lacked, initially

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb was a German missile of the Second World War
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word lacked

explanation.surface: The army lacked a key Second World War missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 is written VI with the numeral as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential, just as something key is crucial.

clue.text: Intellectual, says 14, with facial hair

indicators.note: says 14 means as pronounced by a Cockney from 14 Down, who drops the h

parts.note: a highbrow is an intellectual

explanation.surface: An intellectual Londoner talks about facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney drops the H, so 'ighbrow sounds like the answer; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is the strip of hair growing above each eye.

clue.text: Travellers about to catch fish with type of gun

indicators.note: to catch means the reversed word takes the fish inside
about means the salespeople are turned round

parts.note: reps are travelling sales representatives
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen are about to catch fish using some kind of gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the salespeople into SPER, which then closes round the fish; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray gun, for paint or pesticide, is a common sprayer.
